question: Can a fixed-budget native-local motif learner infer action-conditioned neighbor dependence from sequential public state/action/next-state, then predict unseen transitions and compose multiple steps more accurately than matched no-neighbor and exact-transition-memory controls?
hypothesis: Local factorization allows transfer across global contexts without access to environment rules, but may underperform strong statistical or symbolic controls and is not general intelligence.
predecessor_evidence: WSP63 PR #954 is separate direct weight-editing research and is NOT a parent for this experiment

inputs.name: synthetic four-bit local-ring public step environment
inputs.source: new fixed development-only generator in tests/test_local_causal_motif_dev.py; no outside data, hidden physics or model API exposed to learner

frozen_design.split: 71101-71104 in-family local binary neighbor gates, 71105-71108 deliberately out-of-family self-conditioned gates; all eight are DEV/SELFTEST only, never official protected sources
frozen_design.ordering: one continuous zero-reset, 64 public action-consequence steps per seeded world with action=(step + seed)%4; metrics on all 16 states x 4 actions, strictly excluding observed state/action pairs; no arbitrary-state observations during fit
frozen_design.data_budget: 64 chronological public source steps per world per model; no labels, hidden gate codes, evaluator outcomes or extra synthetic counterfactuals exposed to learner
frozen_design.compute_budget: fixed 64 updates and 64 one-step evaluation queries per world; two-step composition is evaluated from prediction only with no additional training
frozen_design.capacity: four functional cells within 7 active + 9 retained hard-address envelope; exactly 4 learned float64 coefficients per active cell, fixed bounds; no growth, global transition table or external neural model
frozen_design.evaluator: unseen state-action effect correctness and balanced accuracy, 2-action rollout exact-state accuracy on unseen first transitions, cold checkpoint parity and retained no-interference unit checks; record CPU time/peak Python tracked allocations separately

controls: exact global (state,action)->next-state memory (same ledger) with abstention on unknown
trained cell ablative replacement by no-change behavior
metrics: learned float64 count, bytes, steps and wall time

classification_rules.supported: DEV_SIGNAL only if >=12 unseen state/action transitions per in-family world, learned unseen balanced accuracy >=0.70 in each of 4 worlds, >=0.10 absolute above strongest fair control (no-neighbor, always-no-change, exact observed lookup with abstentions scored as errors) averaged over 4, two-step rollout exact rate >=0.60, zero old-skill loss on cold restore and reproducible two-platform focused+full regression. Not a SCIENTIFIC_PASS.
classification_rules.mixed: Any valid nontrivial advantage on a subset but one or more DEV_SIGNAL criteria missed; preserve all failed seed/world values.
classification_rules.negative: Valid run that misses DEV_SIGNAL and does not meet mixed criteria, or is uniformly beaten by a matched control.
classification_rules.invalid: Unfrozen code/identity, source-rule leakage, extra actions, altered seeds or thresholds, contradictory snapshots, missing per-world counts, missing required comparator, or violated fixed budget.

preregistration_note: This commit freezes the prospective development experiment before adding code. No official science evaluation is authorized; stronger independent baselines and authentic-world tests remain mandatory before AGI-related conclusions.
